task: Review the planned no-Stop closeout observer and side-effect mitigation before implementation.
user_intent: Norven wants Cap to implement the mitigations for both old and new side effects of the proposed closeout observer, then reassess which side effects remain unavoidable.
main_claim: The safe design is not a safer Stop hook. It is a no-Stop side-channel observer: it may inspect the previous assistant reply at the next UserPromptSubmit or through an explicit command, write bounded structured records, and expose health through checks. It must never block, never inject a recovery prompt, never return systemMessage/hook_prompt, never invoke LLMs, and never store the full assistant reply.
changed_reality: Stop is no longer deployed in .codex/hooks.json or assets/contracts/codex-hooks.template.json.
UserPromptSubmit still runs automatically at the next user prompt and can perform file-only side effects without rewriting the previous answer.
Final-claim, human-output, terminal-goal, and lifecycle checks already exist as explicit commands.
The planned observer should add bounded observation, retention, health, and self-check coverage without restoring final-reply blocking.
proposal: Add runtime/core/closeout_observer.py with observe, check, and self-check commands.
Persist observations under assets/evidence/closeout-observer/ with a fixed maximum record count, latest summary, and health status.
Store only message hash, length, optional tiny bounded excerpt for diagnostics when safe, and structured risk flags; never store full assistant text.
Use existing final-claim and human-output logic for local deterministic checks, but do not call Prism or any external LLM.

Integrate a file-only observer call into UserPromptSubmit only if a previous assistant reply can be extracted cheaply from transcript_path; failures degrade to health status and never affect additionalContext.
Wire redcap closeout-observer self-check into redcap check and enforcement evidence.
known_constraints: Do not re-add Stop to deployed hooks.
Do not put observer warnings into the assistant context by default.
Do not block or ask the model to rewrite a reply.
Do not run heavyweight checks or provider reviews in the hook path.
Acknowledge that immediate blocking is intentionally not restored.
review_questions: Does this design structurally prevent the old Stop-style answer interference?
Which mitigations are necessary to prevent new noise, privacy, timing, and health blind spots?
What would be the minimum fix if the observer still risks becoming a new workflow nuisance?
expected_output: Return strict JSON with provider, verdict, confidence, reality_delta, main_concern, top_risks, missing_evidence, minimum_fix, anti_loop_signal, and user_intent_alignment.
